name: Pontius Pilate
bio: Luke records that, learning Jesus was a Galilean, Pilate sent him to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem at the time; Herod questioned Jesus, got no answer, mocked him, and sent him back, which reconciled the two rulers, who had previously been at odds (Luke 23:6-12). Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea, questioned Jesus and found no answer when accused by the chief priests. Recognizing the charges were driven by envy and warned by his wife's troubled dream, Pilate offered the crowd a choice between releasing Jesus or the notorious prisoner Barabbas; persuaded by the chief priests, the crowd demanded Barabbas's release and Jesus's crucifixion. Unable to quell the mob, Pilate symbolically washed his hands of responsibility for Jesus's blood, then had him scourged and handed over for crucifixion. He later granted Joseph of Arimathea's request for Jesus's body, and agreed to have the tomb secured and guarded at the chief priests' request (Matthew 27:1-66). John's account of Jesus's trial adds that when Jesus explained his kingdom was not of this world but testified to the truth, Pilate asked, "What is truth?" and then told the Jews he found no fault in Jesus at all (John 18:33-38).
